standard_prerequisites.name: The key formula and infinite sums of rational equivalences
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-key-formula (proof line 5556) and remark-infinite-sums-rational-equivalences (proof line 5568)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the cycle identity turning the difference of the two representatives into a sum of divisors of tame symbols, and lets the resulting rational equivalence pass from the classes [W] to an arbitrary cycle.

core_obligations: Reduce to alpha = [W] for an integral closed subscheme W of delta-dimension k, choosing meromorphic sections sigma of L|_W and sigma' of L'|_W that agree with the respective canonical sections whenever W is not contained in the corresponding divisor, and writing both divisors in coefficient form with local generators at the generic points xi_i (proof lines 5511-5545).

Identify the two composites as cycles built from the same local data: (j')^* i^* [W] is the sum of ord_{B_i}(f_i) div_{L'|Z_i}(sigma'_i|Z_i) and j^* (i')^* [W] is the sum of ord_{B_i}(f'_i) div_{L|Z_i}(sigma_i|Z_i), where sigma = f_i sigma_i and sigma' = f'_i sigma'_i (proof lines 5546-5555).

Apply the key formula to see the difference of those two cycles is the sum of div_{Z_i}(partial_{B_i}(f_i, f'_i)); note that each term vanishes when Z_i is not contained in D intersect D' because then one of f_i, f'_i is 1, so the two representatives are rationally equivalent, and pass from [W] to an arbitrary alpha using the locally finite sums (proof lines 5556-5569).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to one integral class and normalise the two meromorphic sections (proof lines 5511-5545).
Express both composites through the same local generators (proof lines 5546-5555).
Apply the key formula and the vanishing away from the intersection to get the rational equivalence, then extend by locally finite sums (proof lines 5556-5569).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that the two Gysin maps associated with two Cartier divisor triples on X commute, so that the square CH_k(X) -> CH_{k-1}(D) -> CH_{k-2}(D intersect D') agrees with the other way round (statement lines 5495-5508, tag 0B73). The proof reduces to a single integral class, chooses meromorphic sections normalised to agree with the canonical sections away from the divisors, writes both composites as cycles built from the same local generators at the generic points, and then invokes the key formula so that the difference becomes a sum of divisors of tame symbols that vanishes term by term away from the intersection. The local bookkeeping and the passage from [W] to arbitrary cycles are the substance, so the claim is H2.
